scope.flow: FastAccessVault.rebalanceFunds() rebalancing with external custodian transfer
scope.environment: Solidity vault contract with custodian address and ERC777/callback-enabled tokens
evidence: FastAccessVault.rebalanceFunds() Lacks Access Control and Reentrancy Protection, Enabling Griefing and DoS Attacks

The `FastAccessVault.rebalanceFunds()` function has no access control modifier, allowing anyone to trigger vault rebalancing at will. Combined with the external call to the custodian address (which could be a contract), this creates multiple attack vectors:
- Line 176: `_vaultToken.transfer(custodian, excess)` is external call
- No `nonReentrant` modifier on `rebalanceFunds()`
- Malicious custodian contract can re-enter during transfer
- With ERC777 tokens or callback-enabled tokens, can drain excess twice

evidence: The `FastAccessVault.rebalanceFunds()` function has no access control modifier, allowing anyone to trigger vault rebalancing at will. Combined with the external call to the custodian address (which could be a contract), this creates multiple attack vectors:

- Attacker can front-run legitimate rebalancing operations
